resolution_scope: The invalid inference from a false favored explanation to excessive prior confidence is removed. The evaluative defense is strengthened and tested, not made indisputable.
change_summary: Distinguished rational prior confidence from a favored hypothesis that later proves false; specified correction as revising content, not repairing irrationality.
Added a concrete reading of Emma I.VI and I.XV–XVI, with explicit limits on which readers undergo the revision.
Explained aesthetic value through the fit between a work’s treatment of interpretation and the reader’s actual interpretive activity; preserved the strongest informed-imagination objection.

Acknowledged Fish and Iser as close predecessors, bounded Nguyen and Chasid attributions to verified manuscript passages, and preserved realization/replacement/foreclosure and conditional information sequencing.
remaining_issues: The claim that enacted interpretive revision is itself an aesthetically valuable mode remains an evaluative premise; the essay supplies reasons without proving superiority to informed imagination.
The Emma example is a close reading of a possible response, not evidence of its frequency or an empirical experiment.
Whole-article and final-version verification remains incomplete for several sources; exact novelty and priority are unknown.
Independent fresh review of this substantive revision is still required.
costs_or_narrowing: No accusation of irrationality, excessive confidence or defective calibration is made merely because the earlier explanation proves false.
No claim that all uninformed viewers, all actual corrections, or all works realize this good.
No general primacy, mandatory ignorance, fixed authenticity bonus or recommendation against requested guidance.
